subject: EastUS3 phased node swap & warm-restart window — customer outreach
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-14T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: EastUS3 maintenance — proposal for phased node swap and warm-restart window

Team,

We have a narrowed maintenance window proposal for EastUS3 to complete the kernel/driver transition that addresses the increased memory pressure we've been seeing on higher-sequence requests. Summary: a phased node swap with warm-restarts (no full cold boots) across three hostpools over a 6 hour runway next Wednesday (9/22), with canaries in the first 45 minutes. The goals are: preserve KV cache affinity where possible, avoid large tail-latency spikes, and ensure transparent customer communication.

Key asks:
- Marcus: finalize the canary rollout script and the pre-check checklist (KV cache snapshot approach) by EOD Friday.
- Grace/Neha: coordinate customer-facing scheduling and confirm the list of customers with pinned model versions (I want these called out in the outreach).
- Soojin: validate fallback routing and autoscaling triggers for the event (ensure fallback to smaller-quantized model variant is configured).

I've attached a draft playbook and a customer outreach template. I'll take point on executive notifications.

Jordan
Lead, Site Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: eastus3-maintenance-playbook.pdf (doc stub), customer-outreach-template.txt (doc stub)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-runbook@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EastUS3 maintenance — proposal for phased node swap and warm-restart window

Jordan —

Acknowledged. I'll have the canary script and pre-check checklist in the shared drive by Friday morning. Quick notes:
- Plan to snapshot prefix KV hashes for the 30 largest customers (by QPS) and use targeted prefix priming post-restart to warm caches.
- We'll perform the canary on a single hostpool with a synthetic traffic harness that mirrors production token distribution. If we see >2% latency tail increase or >1.5x error rate for LLM generation, we'll abort and roll back.
- Driver changes include a PCIe DMA patch; warm-restart avoids a full reinitialization of the NVMe path so kernel modules are reattached with preserved KV state where possible.

I'll attach the script once validated.

— Marcus
SRE, Serving Runtime

I'll prepare individualized emails and include the rollback criteria and expected customer impact matrix.

Grace

Subject: Planned maintenance: EastUS3 phased node swap and warm-restart (9/22)

Alicia —

I wanted to give you advance notice of a planned maintenance event in our EastUS3 region that may briefly affect requests to any provisioned workloads on that region. We've scheduled a phased node swap and warm-restart window to deploy a kernel/driver update that reduces memory fragmentation and improves long-tail latency for long-sequence generation.

Planned window (proposed):
- UTC: 02:00 — 08:00, Tuesday, 22 Sep 2026
- Local: 10:00 PM — 04:00 AM EDT (Mon/Tue transition)
- Total runway: up to 6 hours. We expect most hostpools to complete within 90–120 minutes each during their stage.

What to expect:
- Short, rolling warm-restarts per hostpool to preserve KV cache where possible. You may see 5–60s of increased latency for affected requests during a hostpool's warm restart; we do not anticipate request failures but will have automatic fallbacks in place.
- We will not change your model versions without explicit consent. If you prefer a pre-warm of KV prefixes (we'll prime the 50 most common prefixes observed in your workload), reply and we'll schedule it before the window.
- If you'd like to opt-out of the EastUS3 window, let us know and we'll discuss alternative options (migrate to a different region or plan an isolated dry-run).

Attachments: maintenance summary and rollback criteria.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Lead, Site Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: eastus3-maintenance-playbook.pdf (doc stub)

Thanks for the heads up, Jordan.

We can do the proposed window, but please schedule the pre-warm — Hyperion's peak usage starts at 14:00 UTC and we'd prefer no impact then. A couple of questions:
1) If you see a canary signal and abort the rollout, how long until you reattempt?
2) Are there any temporary API surface changes we should expect (headers, error codes)?

Also — can you share the post-event metrics dashboard we'll have access to for the follow-up review?

Best,
Alicia Moreno
VP of Platform Engineering
Hyperion Analytics
